DEVELOPER LIBRARY / 04

Runtimes & Execution Platforms.

A runtime turns executable code into work inside a host environment. Distinguish language implementation, virtual machine, engine, host APIs and managed service before comparing products. The pack spans all of these layers, including historical implementations.

ORIENTATION

Roles and responsibilities.

Application developers choose APIs and deployment targets; platform engineers manage execution limits; performance engineers inspect startup, scheduling, memory and foreign interfaces.

How the pieces relate

Source → compiler / interpreter → executable representation
       → runtime + host APIs → operating system / hardware

TECHNICAL GUIDES

Mechanics, tradeoffs and practice.

These are CODARIS editorial explanations. Occupational examples describe engineering responsibilities, not measured demographic shares.

Application runtime versus engine

Technical model

Node.js combines a JavaScript engine with host APIs, module loading and asynchronous I/O. V8 is an engine, not the complete Node application environment. Browser code and server code can share syntax while having different capabilities and globals.

Failure modes and decisions

Do not infer API compatibility from a shared engine. Test filesystem, networking, module resolution and native dependencies on the actual target. An engine benchmark does not include the cost of the whole service.

Practice task

Draw the host boundary for a script that reads a file and serves its contents. List which capabilities a browser would not expose directly.

https://nodejs.org/en/learn/getting-started/introduction-to-nodejs ↗

Bytecode, JIT and ahead-of-time compilation

Technical model

Managed execution may compile source into an intermediate representation, interpret it or compile hot paths during execution. Ahead-of-time compilation moves work before deployment. The JVM specification and a particular JVM implementation are different things.

Failure modes and decisions

Startup, warmup, code size and steady-state throughput are separate measurements. Native output can still depend on runtime libraries; ahead-of-time compilation is not a promise of zero runtime support.

Practice task

Design a benchmark with separate cold-start and warmed-up phases. Record runtime configuration and explain why the results may differ.

https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/ ↗

Memory management and resource ownership

Technical model

Garbage collection finds memory that is no longer reachable. Ownership and reference-counting models make different lifetime tradeoffs. File descriptors, database handles and native allocations may require explicit cleanup regardless of the language memory model.

Failure modes and decisions

A reachable object graph can grow forever without violating memory safety. Measure retained memory and allocation rate separately. Ensure cancellation also releases non-memory resources.

Practice task

Trace the lifetime of a request buffer and a socket through success, timeout and cancellation paths.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/garbage-collection/ ↗

WebAssembly and host capabilities

Technical model

WebAssembly defines an executable instruction format. A concrete runtime validates and runs modules; imported functions provide access to the host. WASI supplies families of system interfaces rather than naming one execution engine.

Failure modes and decisions

A sandbox is only as restricted as its exposed capabilities and resource budgets. Validate imports, bound memory and execution, and review any host function that can access files or networks.

Practice task

Compile a pure function to Wasm, list its imports, and explain which extra host function would change its trust boundary.

https://webassembly.org/docs/high-level-goals/ ↗

Scheduling, blocking and backpressure

Technical model

Event loops, threads, workers and asynchronous tasks organize concurrent work differently. Waiting asynchronously can free an execution thread, while CPU-heavy synchronous work can delay unrelated requests. Queues connect producers and consumers.

Failure modes and decisions

Concurrency does not imply unlimited capacity. Bound queues, propagate cancellation and decide how overload is signalled. Moving work to a worker pool still needs queue limits and shutdown handling.

Practice task

Sketch a producer that receives 200 jobs per second and a consumer that completes 100. Define what happens after its queue fills.

https://nodejs.org/en/learn/asynchronous-work/dont-block-the-event-loop ↗

Runtime selection and operational compatibility

Technical model

Choose using required libraries, deployment architecture, observability, support policy and workload behavior. Embedded, browser, accelerator and serverless contexts impose different limits. Imported version/status facts are dated snapshots, not installation recommendations.

Failure modes and decisions

Check native ABI dependencies, architecture support and upgrade rollback. Managed services can restrict execution duration, memory or filesystem persistence even when they run a familiar language.

Practice task

Write a compatibility matrix for one application on a local process, container and managed function. Include startup, state, networking and debugging.

https://docs.wasmtime.dev/ ↗

Key Relationships
Key_Relationships
TechnologyWhat it isRuns on / usesCommon relationshipCODARIS teaching point
Node.jsJavaScript application runtimeV8JavaScript -> Node.js -> V8 -> native machine codeNode.js is not the JavaScript engine; V8 is its primary execution engine.
DenoJavaScript/TypeScript/Wasm runtimeV8TypeScript types stripped -> JavaScript -> V8Deno adds runtime APIs, tooling and permissions around V8.
BunJavaScript/TypeScript runtime + toolchainJavaScriptCoreJavaScript/TypeScript -> Bun -> JavaScriptCoreBun does not use V8.
Chrome / ChromiumBrowser execution platformV8Web page JavaScript -> V8Browser runtime includes far more than the language engine.
FirefoxBrowser execution platformSpiderMonkeyWeb page JavaScript -> SpiderMonkeySpiderMonkey is Mozilla's JS engine.
Safari / WebKitBrowser execution platformJavaScriptCoreWeb page JavaScript -> JavaScriptCoreJavaScriptCore is WebKit's JS VM.
Java applicationManaged JVM applicationHotSpot / OpenJ9 / another JVMJava/Kotlin/etc -> JVM bytecode -> JVM -> native executionJVM is a specification with multiple implementations.
.NET applicationManaged CLI applicationCoreCLR / Mono / NativeAOTC#/F#/VB -> CIL -> runtime/JIT or AOT -> nativeCLR/CoreCLR and .NET are related but not identical labels.
Elixir applicationBEAM ecosystem applicationBEAM / ERTSElixir -> BEAM bytecode -> BEAMElixir is a language; BEAM is the VM.
Python applicationPython programCPython / PyPy / Jython / IronPython / GraalPyPython source -> implementation-specific execution'Python' does not imply one runtime in every environment.
WebAssembly modulePortable binary moduleWasmtime / Wasmer / WasmEdge / browser engine / othersLanguage compiler -> Wasm -> runtimeWasm is a binary instruction format, not itself a standalone runtime.
WASI componentPortable system-facing Wasm componentWASI-capable Wasm runtimeWasm component -> WASI interfaces -> host capabilitiesWASI defines interfaces/capabilities; the runtime enforces execution.

Methodology
Methodology
IssueCODARIS treatmentWhy it matters
Runtime vs engineStore separate Runtime Type and Engine/Host Relation fields.Node.js is a runtime built on V8; Bun is a runtime built on JavaScriptCore; an engine is not the whole application runtime.
VM specification vs implementationTreat JVM as a VM/specification family and HotSpot/OpenJ9/GraalVM as implementations/runtime distributions.Prevents duplicate or misleading statements such as 'Java runs only on HotSpot'.
Managed vs native runtimeInclude managed VMs and native language runtime systems, but label execution model and bytecode/IR.Go, Haskell and Swift can have substantial runtimes even though application code is compiled to native code.
WebAssemblySeparate WebAssembly/WASI standards from concrete runtimes such as Wasmtime, Wasmer, WasmEdge and WAMR.Wasm is an instruction format; WASI is a system-interface family; runtimes execute them.
Browser execution contextsKeep Browser, Service Worker, Web Worker and Worklet entries as execution environments, not language engines.State of JS explicitly measures some of these as JavaScript runtimes, but technically they sit above the JS engine.
Edge/serverless runtimesInclude major provider execution platforms but label them Managed execution platform.They are relevant developer runtimes but also overlap the later CODARIS Cloud/Hosting category.
State of JS usageUse the 2025 selections and calculated share of question respondents. Multi-select percentages can sum above 100%.This is survey adoption among JavaScript-community respondents, not a global runtime market share.
Stack Overflow usageOnly include Node.js and Deno values where the Stack Overflow 2025 web-technologies question directly measured them.Its denominator/question differs from State of JS, so values are not merged.
Country and genderDo not infer runtime-by-country or runtime-by-gender shares from overall survey demographics.Direct cross-tab data is required for defensible demographic claims.
CompletenessDescribe this as an extensive curated catalogue of 581 entries, not every runtime ever built.Runtime terminology overlaps engines, VMs, libraries, runtimes, historical implementations, research VMs, cloud execution contexts and hardware accelerators.

RESEARCH INTEGRITY

Scope and demographic limits.

Project
CODARIS Runtimes & Execution Platforms educational research dataset
Generated date
2026-09-23
Catalogue count
581
Scope
Extensive curated A-Z catalogue of language runtimes, virtual machines, JavaScript engines, WebAssembly runtimes, managed runtimes, native runtime systems, browser contexts, edge/serverless execution platforms, embedded runtimes and accelerator runtimes.
Taxonomy warning
A language runtime, VM implementation, JavaScript engine, runtime library and managed serverless execution platform are different layers. CODARIS should keep runtime_type, family and engine/host relations visible.
Usage warning
State of JS and Stack Overflow metrics use different survey populations and questions. Do not combine them into one universal runtime market-share score.

Survey respondents are not a census of all developers. A country’s overall respondent share cannot establish tool use within that country. No per-tool gender percentages are inferred; defensible cross-tabs need direct evidence, sample sizes, year and the source’s complete response categories.

These categories overlap. A tool can serve several roles, so total catalogue rows do not equal globally unique technologies. Version and product-status notes describe the supplied snapshot date; check primary documentation before adopting or upgrading.

PROVENANCE

Follow the research.

Original JSON, CSVs, workbook and README are preserved in the repository. Their checksums are recorded in the companion SHA256SUMS integrity manifest. Source terms and attribution remain applicable. Editorial guides are separate from imported research.

Original source-pack README
# CODARIS Runtimes & Execution Platforms Research Pack

Generated: 23 September 2026

## Scope

This research pack contains **581 runtime and execution-platform entries**.

The catalogue intentionally spans several layers because developers use the word "runtime" for different things:

- application runtimes such as Node.js, Deno and Bun
- language engines such as V8, SpiderMonkey and JavaScriptCore
- managed virtual machines such as JVM, HotSpot, OpenJ9 and CLR/CoreCLR
- language implementations such as CPython, PyPy, JRuby and LuaJIT
- runtime systems linked into native applications such as Go Runtime and GHC RTS
- WebAssembly runtimes such as Wasmtime, Wasmer, WasmEdge, WAMR and wazero
- browser execution environments such as Service Workers and Web Workers
- edge/serverless execution platforms such as Cloudflare Workers and AWS Lambda
- embedded runtimes
- GPU/accelerator runtimes such as CUDA Runtime

CODARIS should show **Runtime Type**, **Runtime Family**, and **Engine / Host Relation** prominently.

## Key architecture examples

### Node.js

JavaScript / TypeScript application
→ Node.js runtime
→ V8 JavaScript engine
→ JIT/native machine execution

Node.js is **not** the same thing as V8.

### Deno

JavaScript / TypeScript
→ Deno runtime and APIs
→ V8
→ native execution

Deno adds a permission model, tooling, module system and runtime APIs around V8.

### Bun

JavaScript / TypeScript
→ Bun runtime/toolchain
→ JavaScriptCore
→ native execution

Bun does **not** use V8.

### Java / Kotlin on JVM

Java/Kotlin/etc.
→ JVM bytecode
→ a JVM implementation such as HotSpot, OpenJ9 or GraalVM
→ native execution

The JVM is a virtual-machine specification/family. HotSpot is one important implementation, not the only one.

### .NET

C#/F#/VB
→ CIL
→ CoreCLR/CLR/Mono or NativeAOT
→ native execution

NativeAOT changes the deployment/execution model by compiling IL to native code before runtime.

### WebAssembly

Rust/C/C++/Go/etc.
→ WebAssembly module/component
→ Wasmtime/Wasmer/WasmEdge/browser engine/etc.
→ host machine

Wasm is a binary instruction format. WASI defines portable system-facing interfaces. Neither is itself a single runtime implementation.

## State of JavaScript 2025 runtime usage

The JavaScript Runtimes question had **11,141 respondents** and allowed multiple selections.

- Node.js: 10,062 selections, **90.3%**
- Browser: 9,682, **86.9%**
- Bun: 2,321, **20.8%**
- Service Workers: 1,660, **14.9%**
- Cloudflare Workers: 1,294, **11.6%**
- Deno: 1,244, **11.2%**
- Hermes: 354, **3.2%**
- ChakraCore: 33, **0.3%**

These numbers describe State of JavaScript respondents, not worldwide market share.

The separate edge/serverless runtime question had **9,593 respondents**.

## Current snapshots

The workbook includes selected current-version/status facts verified for 23 September 2026, including Node.js release status, the Java SE 27 JVM specification, OpenJ9's September 2026 release, MicroPython, WASI milestones and CUDA Runtime documentation.

## Geography and demographics

No runtime-by-country or runtime-by-gender percentages are fabricated.

Overall Stack Overflow survey geography is included only as sample context. A country's respondent share does not tell us which runtime developers in that country use.

## Files

- `CODARIS_runtimes_execution_platforms_research.xlsx`
- `codaris_runtimes_execution_platforms_catalog.csv`
- `codaris_runtimes_execution_platforms_catalog.json`
- `codaris_runtime_usage_stateofjs_2025.csv`
- `codaris_edge_runtime_usage_stateofjs_2025.csv`
- `codaris_runtimes_sources.csv`

## Recommended CODARIS fields

1. Runtime / execution platform name
2. Runtime family
3. Runtime type
4. Languages / executable format
5. Execution model
6. Bytecode / IR
7. Memory-management model
8. Typical environment
9. Sandbox / isolation model
10. Provider or project
11. Engine / host relationship
12. Usage metric plus source/year where available
13. Notes
14. Source provenance

Do not create one synthetic "runtime popularity score" by averaging unrelated survey, download, website, GitHub or vendor metrics.
